title: Spin-1 teleportation-based quantum state tomography
abstract: We show that the teleportation-based quantum state tomography (QST) protocol, originally built to reconstruct qubits (spin-1/2 systems), can be extended to deal with qutrits (spin-1 systems) as well. Similarly to the original proposal, only two resources are needed to implement the spin-1 teleportation-based QST protocol: (1) Alice should be able to implement the analog of Bell measurements for spin-1 systems; and (2) she should be able to prepare a few different single qutrit states that will be teleported to Bob.
summary: This paper extends the teleportation-based Quantum State Tomography protocol from qubits to qutrits (spin-1 systems). It demonstrates that by performing multiple quantum teleportation experiments using nine distinct input states, one can fully reconstruct the density matrix of a two-qutrit system. The method is shown to scale systematically to $n$-qutrits, providing a powerful theoretical tool for characterizing high-dimensional quantum states.
main_problem: The primary goal is extending the quantum state tomography protocol, originally designed for qubits (spin-1/2), to reconstruct arbitrary states of qutrits (spin-1 systems). This extends to higher dimensions ($n$-qutrits) as well.
main_result: The protocol successfully determines the density matrix $\rho_{12}$ (for two qutrits) by performing multiple quantum teleportation experiments using nine distinct known input states. The method scales to $n$-qutrits, requiring $9^{n-1}$ such experiments.
method: The reconstruction relies on measuring the resulting single-qutrit state ($ho_2$) at Bob's end after Alice performs a Bell measurement on her two qubits (the unknown system and an auxiliary qubit). A consistent set of linear equations is solved using these measurements to determine the density matrix elements.
model_or_system: The physical system involves qutrits, which are spin-1 systems ($	ext{dim}=3$). The process models quantum state tomography on a two-qutrit system $\rho_{12}$ by leveraging the principles of quantum teleportation.
key_observables: The matrix elements ($m_{ij}$) of the unknown density matrix $\rho_{12}$, and the probabilities ($Q_j$) associated with various Bell measurement outcomes.
important_parameters: The number of required input states scales exponentially, $9^{n-1}$, for an $n$-qutrit system. The reconstruction requires at least nine distinct teleportation measurements for two qutrits.
main_assumptions: It is assumed that Bob can experimentally reconstruct his single-qutrit density matrix ($ho_2$) using standard QST methods, and the protocol assumes specific measurement outcomes (e.g., measuring $|B_1\rangle$ initially).
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the general teleportation-based QST protocol for two qutrits. Figure 3 extends this concept to three qutrits, showing Alice preparing and projecting pairs of states onto Bell bases.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the extension from qubits to qutrits, detailing the required measurements (nine input states). It then provides explicit formulas relating the unknown density matrix elements ($\rho_{12}$) to Bob's measured single-qutrit states. Finally, it discusses the general scaling of this method to $n$-qutrits.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it develops a concrete, scalable protocol for characterizing multi-partite quantum states in higher-dimensional systems (qutrits), which are crucial testbeds for understanding entanglement beyond simple qubit models.
